title: Log onset had a larger within-source distance slope than log rise in Allen mouse inhibitory outputs with unknown target classes kept
abstract: We tested whether cell-body distance has a larger proportional relation with response onset time than with voltage rise time within outputs from one source cell. We used linked connection and response records in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 small data. The primary mouse visual-cortex inhibitory sample had 278 connections from 129 source cells and 97 inferred donors. We matched source cell and target class. The log-onset slope was 0.269 per 100 micrometres. The log-rise slope was 0.020. Their paired difference was 0.249, with a nominal 95% donor bootstrap interval of 0.059 to 0.432. The interval excluded zero. Removing unknown target classes made the contrast interval include zero. The absolute-time contrast was also uncertain. This extends earlier separate timing analyses of the same release. It does not identify axon speed, contact location, or causation. Selected slice connections, inferred donor labels, unknown response-fit errors, and a small human sample limit transfer. Code, selected records, donor statistics, uncertainty draws, and checks are supplied.

display.caption: Paired distance slopes on a log time scale. Only the mouse inhibitory onset-minus-rise contrast is primary. Bars give nominal 95% donor bootstrap intervals.

citations.reason: Prior within-source delay result supplies the comparison design; this report adds a paired onset-versus-rise contrast.
Prior rise-time prediction test motivates a direct paired comparison.
